files.content:
# Functional Requirements for Todo List Application

## User Authentication

### Registration

- Users can register with an email address and password.
- Users must verify their email address before they can log in.
- Users must provide a unique username.
- Users must agree to the terms and conditions.

### Login

- Users can log in with their email address and password.
- Users can log in with their username and password.
- Users can log in with their social media accounts.
- Users can reset their password if they forget it.

### Logout

- Users can log out of their account.
- Users are prompted to confirm before logging out.

### Password Management

- Users can change their password.
- Users can reset their password if they forget it.
- Users must provide their current password to change it.
- Users must provide a new password and confirm it.

## Todo Item Management

### Create Todo Item

- Users can create a new todo item.
- Users must provide a title for the todo item.
- Users can provide a description for the todo item.
- Users can set a due date for the todo item.
- Users can set a priority level for the todo item.

### Read Todo Items

- Users can view a list of their todo items.
- Users can filter their todo items by status (completed, pending).
- Users can sort their todo items by due date, priority, or creation date.

### Update Todo Item

- Users can update the title, description, due date, and priority level of a todo item.
- Users can mark a todo item as completed.
- Users can unmark a completed todo item.

### Delete Todo Item

- Users can delete a todo item.
- Users are prompted to confirm before deleting a todo item.

## User Interface

### Home Screen

- The home screen displays a welcome message and a list of recent todo items.
- The home screen provides quick access to the todo list screen and settings screen.

### Todo List Screen

- The todo list screen displays a list of all todo items.
- The todo list screen provides options to filter and sort the todo items.
- The todo list screen provides a button to create a new todo item.

### Todo Item Screen

- The todo item screen displays the details of a todo item.
- The todo item screen provides options to update and delete the todo item.

### Settings Screen

- The settings screen provides options to manage user account settings.
- The settings screen provides options to manage application settings.

## Data Storage

### Database Schema

- The database schema includes tables for users, todo items, and user sessions.
- The database schema includes relationships between users and todo items.

### Data Persistence

- User data is persisted in the database.
- Todo item data is persisted in the database.

### Data Synchronization

- User data is synchronized across devices.
- Todo item data is synchronized across devices.

## Error Handling

### Error Types

- Authentication errors (invalid credentials, account locked).
- Validation errors (invalid input, missing required fields).
- Database errors (connection issues, query failures).

### Error Messages

- Error messages are displayed to the user in a user-friendly format.
- Error messages provide guidance on how to resolve the error.

### Error Recovery

- Users can retry failed operations.
- Users can contact support for assistance.

## Performance Requirements

### Response Time

- The application should respond to user actions within 2 seconds.

### Throughput

- The application should handle 1000 concurrent users.

### Scalability

- The application should scale to handle 1 million users.

## Additional Notes

- This document provides a detailed specification of the Todo list application, including user flows and technical considerations.
- It serves as a comprehensive guide for the development team to ensure all aspects of the application are covered.
- The target audience is the development team, who will use this document to guide the development process.

models.name: todo_list_configurations
models.description:
System-wide configuration settings for the todo list application.

Stores application-wide settings that control behavior and appearance of the
application. These configurations apply across all users and devices, providing
centralized control over system behavior.

Configuration settings include:

- Application name and branding
- Default settings for new users
- Feature toggles for experimental features
- System-wide limits and constraints
- Integration settings with external services

The configuration table serves as a central repository for system-wide
settings that can be modified by administrators to control application behavior
without requiring code changes.

This table is critical for maintaining consistent behavior across the
application and enabling centralized administration of system-wide parameters.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Unique identifier for the configuration setting.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Value of the configuration setting.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of the configuration setting.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the configuration setting. Valid values: active, inactive.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the configuration setting was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the configuration setting was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the configuration setting was deleted (soft delete).

models.name: todo_list_users
models.description:
User accounts for the todo list application.

Stores core user information including authentication credentials and
account status. Each user has a unique email address and username.
Passwords are stored as secure hashes. Users can have multiple login
methods (email, username, social media).

Supports soft deletion to allow account recovery while maintaining audit
trails. Includes timestamps for account creation and last update.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: User's email address for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all users.

plainFields.name: username
plainFields.description: User's chosen username for authentication. Must be unique across all users.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Secure hash of user's password. Never store plain text passwords.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was soft-deleted. Null if account is active.

models.name: todo_list_user_sessions
models.description:
User session records for tracking active user sessions.

Stores information about active user sessions including IP address, connection
context, and session duration. Each session is associated with a specific
user account and session type.

Supports session expiration and provides audit trail for user activity.
Includes timestamps for session creation and expiration.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: User account associated with this session. {@link todo_list_users.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the page where the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led to the session initiation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expired or was terminated. Null if session is active.

models.name: todo_list_user_email_logins
models.description:
Email login records for user authentication.

Stores information about successful email logins including IP address and
connection context. Each login record is associated with a specific user
account.

Provides audit trail for user authentication activity. Includes
timestamps for login attempts.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: User account associated with this login. {@link todo_list_users.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the login attempt was made.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the page where the login attempt was initiated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led to the login attempt.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the login attempt was recorded.

models.name: todo_list_user_username_logins
models.description:
Username login records for user authentication.

Stores information about successful username logins including IP address and
connection context. Each login record is associated with a specific user
account.

Provides audit trail for user authentication activity. Includes
timestamps for login attempts.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: User account associated with this login. {@link todo_list_users.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the login attempt was made.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the page where the login attempt was initiated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led to the login attempt.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the login attempt was recorded.

models.name: todo_list_user_social_media_logins
models.description:
Social media login records for user authentication.

Stores information about successful social media logins including provider
information, IP address, and connection context. Each login record is
associated with a specific user account.

Provides audit trail for user authentication activity. Includes
timestamps for login attempts.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: User account associated with this login. {@link todo_list_users.id}

plainFields.name: provider
plainFields.description: Social media provider used for authentication (e.g., 'google', 'facebook').

plainFields.name: provider_id
plainFields.description: Unique identifier provided by the social media provider for the user.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the login attempt was made.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the page where the login attempt was initiated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led to the login attempt.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the login attempt was recorded.

models.name: todo_list_user_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset records for user account recovery.

Stores information about password reset requests including reset token, IP
address, and connection context. Each reset record is associated with a
specific user account.

Provides audit trail for password reset activity. Includes timestamps
for reset requests and completions.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: User account associated with this password reset. {@link todo_list_users.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Secure token for password reset verification. Must be unique and time-limited.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the password reset request was made.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the page where the password reset request was initiated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led to the password reset request.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset request was created.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset was completed. Null if reset is pending.

models.name: todo_list_todo_items
models.description:
Core todo item entity representing tasks that users need to complete.

Stores the fundamental task information including title, description, and due date.
Each todo item is associated with a specific user and has a status and priority.
Supports soft deletion to allow for task recovery and history tracking.

This entity forms the central focus of the todo list application, allowing users to
manage their tasks through creation, modification, and completion tracking.
The todo item maintains relationships with user accounts, status types, and
priority levels to provide comprehensive task management capabilities.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: User who owns this todo item. {@link todo_list_users.id}

foreignFields.name: todo_list_todo_item_status_id
foreignFields.description: Current status of this todo item. {@link todo_list_todo_item_statuses.id}

foreignFields.name: todo_list_todo_item_priority_id
foreignFields.description: Priority level of this todo item. {@link todo_list_todo_item_priorities.id}

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Title of the todo item. Must be between 1 and 100 characters.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the todo item. Can be up to 1000 characters.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Date and time when the todo item is due. Must be in the future.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo item was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo item was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo item was soft-deleted. Null if not deleted.

models.name: todo_list_todo_item_statuses
models.description:
Enumeration of possible statuses for todo items.

Defines the lifecycle states that todo items can transition through, providing
clear visibility into task progress. Statuses include pending, in-progress,
completed, and archived, allowing users to track task completion and
prioritize their workload effectively.

This entity serves as a reference table for todo item statuses, enabling
consistent status management across the application. The predefined status
values ensure standardized task tracking and reporting capabilities.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Name of the status. Must be one of: pending, in-progress, completed, archived.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the status meaning and usage.

models.name: todo_list_todo_item_priorities
models.description:
Enumeration of possible priority levels for todo items.

Defines the importance levels that can be assigned to todo items, allowing
users to prioritize their tasks effectively. Priority levels include low,
medium, high, and critical, enabling clear task prioritization and
workload management.

This entity serves as a reference table for todo item priorities, enabling
consistent priority management across the application. The predefined priority
levels ensure standardized task prioritization and reporting capabilities.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Name of the priority level. Must be one of: low, medium, high, critical.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the priority level meaning and usage.

### `todo_list_configurations`

System-wide configuration settings for the todo list application.

Stores application-wide settings that control behavior and appearance of the
application. These configurations apply across all users and devices,
providing
centralized control over system behavior.

Configuration settings include:

- Application name and branding
- Default settings for new users
- Feature toggles for experimental features
- System-wide limits and constraints
- Integration settings with external services

The configuration table serves as a central repository for system-wide
settings that can be modified by administrators to control application
behavior
without requiring code changes.

This table is critical for maintaining consistent behavior across the
application and enabling centralized administration of system-wide
parameters.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `key`: Unique identifier for the configuration setting.
- `value`: Value of the configuration setting.
- `description`: Human-readable description of the configuration setting.
- `status`
  > Current status of the configuration setting. Valid values: active,
  > inactive.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the configuration setting was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the configuration setting was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the configuration setting was deleted (soft delete).

### `todo_list_users`

User accounts for the todo list application.

Stores core user information including authentication credentials and
account status. Each user has a unique email address and username.
Passwords are stored as secure hashes. Users can have multiple login
methods (email, username, social media).

Supports soft deletion to allow account recovery while maintaining audit
trails. Includes timestamps for account creation and last update.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > User's email address for authentication and communication. Must be unique
  > across all users.
- `username`
  > User's chosen username for authentication. Must be unique across all
  > users.
- `password_hash`: Secure hash of user's password. Never store plain text passwords.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the user account was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the user account was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the user account was soft-deleted. Null if account is
  > active.

### `todo_list_user_sessions`

User session records for tracking active user sessions.

Stores information about active user sessions including IP address,
connection
context, and session duration. Each session is associated with a specific
user account and session type.

Supports session expiration and provides audit trail for user activity.
Includes timestamps for session creation and expiration.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_list_user_id`: User account associated with this session. [todo_list_users.id](#todo_list_users)
- `ip`: IP address from which the session was initiated.
- `href`: URL of the page where the session was initiated.
- `referrer`: Referrer URL that led to the session initiation.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the session was created.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when the session expired or was terminated. Null if session is
  > active.

Email login records for user authentication.

Stores information about successful email logins including IP address and
connection context. Each login record is associated with a specific user
account.

Provides audit trail for user authentication activity. Includes
timestamps for login attempts.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_list_user_id`: User account associated with this login. [todo_list_users.id](#todo_list_users)
- `ip`: IP address from which the login attempt was made.
- `href`: URL of the page where the login attempt was initiated.
- `referrer`: Referrer URL that led to the login attempt.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the login attempt was recorded.

### `todo_list_user_username_logins`

Username login records for user authentication.

Stores information about successful username logins including IP address and
connection context. Each login record is associated with a specific user
account.

Provides audit trail for user authentication activity. Includes
timestamps for login attempts.

Properties as follows:

- `ip`: IP address from which the login attempt was made.
- `href`: URL of the page where the login attempt was initiated.
- `referrer`: Referrer URL that led to the login attempt.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the login attempt was recorded.

### `todo_list_user_social_media_logins`

Social media login records for user authentication.

Stores information about successful social media logins including provider
information, IP address, and connection context. Each login record is
associated with a specific user account.

Provides audit trail for user authentication activity. Includes
timestamps for login attempts.

Properties as follows:

- `todo_list_user_id`: User account associated with this login. [todo_list_users.id](#todo_list_users)
- `provider`
  > Social media provider used for authentication (e.g., 'google',

- `provider_id`: Unique identifier provided by the social media provider for the user.
- `ip`: IP address from which the login attempt was made.
- `href`: URL of the page where the login attempt was initiated.
- `referrer`: Referrer URL that led to the login attempt.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the login attempt was recorded.

Password reset records for user account recovery.

Stores information about password reset requests including reset token, IP
address, and connection context. Each reset record is associated with a
specific user account.

Provides audit trail for password reset activity. Includes timestamps
for reset requests and completions.

Properties as follows:

  > User account associated with this password reset. {@link

- `referrer`: Referrer URL that led to the password reset request.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the password reset request was created.
- `completed_at`: Timestamp when the password reset was completed. Null if reset is pending.

### `todo_list_todo_items`

Core todo item entity representing tasks that users need to complete.

Stores the fundamental task information including title, description, and
due date.
Each todo item is associated with a specific user and has a status and
priority.
Supports soft deletion to allow for task recovery and history tracking.

This entity forms the central focus of the todo list application,
allowing users to
manage their tasks through creation, modification, and completion tracking.
The todo item maintains relationships with user accounts, status types, and
priority levels to provide comprehensive task management capabilities.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_list_user_id`: User who owns this todo item. [todo_list_users.id](#todo_list_users)
- `todo_list_todo_item_status_id`: Current status of this todo item. [todo_list_todo_item_statuses.id](#todo_list_todo_item_statuses)
- `todo_list_todo_item_priority_id`
  > Priority level of this todo item. {@link
  > todo_list_todo_item_priorities.id}
- `title`: Title of the todo item. Must be between 1 and 100 characters.
- `description`: Detailed description of the todo item. Can be up to 1000 characters.
- `due_date`: Date and time when the todo item is due. Must be in the future.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the todo item was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the todo item was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the todo item was soft-deleted. Null if not deleted.

### `todo_list_todo_item_statuses`

Enumeration of possible statuses for todo items.

Defines the lifecycle states that todo items can transition through,
providing
clear visibility into task progress. Statuses include pending, in-progress,
completed, and archived, allowing users to track task completion and
prioritize their workload effectively.

This entity serves as a reference table for todo item statuses, enabling
consistent status management across the application. The predefined status
values ensure standardized task tracking and reporting capabilities.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `name`
  > Name of the status. Must be one of: pending, in-progress, completed,
  > archived.
- `description`: Detailed description of the status meaning and usage.

### `todo_list_todo_item_priorities`

Enumeration of possible priority levels for todo items.

Defines the importance levels that can be assigned to todo items, allowing
users to prioritize their tasks effectively. Priority levels include low,
medium, high, and critical, enabling clear task prioritization and
workload management.

This entity serves as a reference table for todo item priorities, enabling
consistent priority management across the application. The predefined
priority
levels ensure standardized task prioritization and reporting capabilities.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `name`: Name of the priority level. Must be one of: low, medium, high, critical.
- `description`: Detailed description of the priority level meaning and usage.
